function.name: bash
function.description: Default shell tool on macOS/Linux; BACKUP ONLY on Windows: prefer `powershell` for all shell work. On Windows, use `bash` only when a command genuinely needs a Unix tool that PowerShell lacks. Execute a shell command in the current working directory (bash on Unix; {shell_note}). Returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Non-zero exit codes are reported. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds (default 120). Pass background=true to fire and forget a long command; its result comes back later as a message. A call still running after 30 seconds is moved to the background automatically (same delivery) — pass a timeout long enough for the work; it still applies to a backgrounded call.

background.description: true = do not wait: returns at once with a task id while the command keeps running. Its output arrives later as a message tagged [inbox from task], and the full output is at output/tasks/<id>.log (read it with the read tool). Set timeout to the long budget you want, e.g. 3600. Use for anything that takes minutes.
